answer:
The simulation uses interFoam in 2D (x-y plane) to model gravity-driven sloshing in a fixed, open-top rectangular tank.
The physical tank dimensions are 1.0 m (x) by 0.6 m (y) by 0.1 m (z); the mesh resolves only x and y with a single cell in z.
The mesh is generated with blockMesh using nCells (200 120 1) and a single block spanning (0 0 0) to (1.0 0.6 0.1).
The frontAndBack boundaries are of type empty in blockMeshDict and in all field files.
The bottom (y=0), left (x=0), and right (x=1.0) boundaries are stationary noSlip walls.
The top boundary (y=0.6) is open to the atmosphere: U uses pressureInletOutletVelocity with value (0 0 0); p_rgh uses totalPressure with p0 0, U U, rho rho, psi phi, value 0; alpha.water uses inletOutlet with inletValue 0 and value 0.
Gravity is set to (0 -9.81 0) in constant/g.
The initial velocity field U is uniformly (0 0 0) everywhere.
The initial p_rgh field is uniformly 0 everywhere.
The initial alpha.water field is 0 everywhere except inside ten staircase slices defined in setFields via boxToCell.
Each boxToCell slice is 0.1 m wide in x, spans z from 0 to 0.1, and has a water height equal to the midpoint depth of that slice: slice i (i=0 to 9) covers x from i*0.1 to (i+1)*0.1 and y from 0 to (0.255 + i*0.01).
The ten boxToCell boxes are: (0 0 0)(0.1 0.255 0.1), (0.1 0 0)(0.2 0.265 0.1), (0.2 0 0)(0.3 0.275 0.1), (0.3 0 0)(0.4 0.285 0.1), (0.4 0 0)(0.5 0.295 0.1), (0.5 0 0)(0.6 0.305 0.1), (0.6 0 0)(0.7 0.315 0.1), (0.7 0 0)(0.8 0.325 0.1), (0.8 0 0)(0.9 0.335 0.1), (0.9 0 0)(1.0 0.345 0.1), each setting alpha.water to 1.
The fluid pair is water (rho 1000, nu 1e-6) and air (rho 1.225, nu 1.5e-5) with surface tension sigma 0.073 N/m.
The controlDict sets endTime 10, deltaT 1e-3, adjustTimeStep yes, maxCo 0.5, and writeInterval 0.05.
No moving reference frame, no external forcing, no rotational acceleration, and no amplitude forcing are applied; the only excitation is the initial tilted free surface.
The simulation is purely transient and gravity-driven, relying on the initial geometric imbalance to drive the sloshing oscillation.
